title: Search job
description: A divided search, pinned by hash. A job document says what walk every contributor runs and what shape a unit of its output takes; its SHA-256 over canonical `tag=value` lines is the job id, and a piecework objective's checker carries that id, so the job is inside the objective's own id. Nothing here is a cairn record: the log never carries a job document, the checker does, and this file exists so two implementations of the same walk agree about what they are running. See docs/design/rho-piecework.md (version 1) and docs/design/orbit-piecework.md (version 2).

hex.description: Lowercase hex, no prefix, no leading zero. One value, one spelling: the job id is a hash of these strings, so `0a` and `a` would be two different jobs with the same parameters.

v1.title: Version 1: r-adding walk on a prime-field curve
v1.description: The shape `examples/certicom-ecdlp/jobs/{nums-50,eccp131}-rho.json` are written in and `tools/rho_dp.py` runs. A point on `y^2 = x^3 + ax + b` over `F_p` carries its own coefficients `(a, b)` with `aP + bQ = (x, y)`, so a distinguished point is its own certificate and the artifact needs nothing else. Frozen: these job ids are inside shipped checkers, and a field added here would move them.

target.description: Q, whose logarithm base P is the answer.

order.description: n, the prime order of P.

dp_bits.description: A point is distinguished when the low `dp_bits` bits of x are zero, so a trail is about 2^dp_bits steps.

num_branches.description: Size of the r-adding branch table, derived from the job id.

negation_map.description: Fold each point to the representative with 2y <= p, halving the search at the cost of fruitless cycles the walk must escape.

unit_size.description: Walker indices per unit of the work assignment.

max_steps_per_walker.description: Step cap before a trail is abandoned; 0 means the implementation's default of 20 * 2^dp_bits.

seed.description: Domain separator mixed into every derived scalar.

v2.title: Version 2: Frobenius-adding walk on a binary Koblitz curve, paid per orbit
v2.description:
ECC2K-130's shape. Three things make it a different document rather than a field added to version 1, and each of them changes what a unit IS.

First, the equivalence group. On `y^2 + xy = x^3 + ax^2 + b` over `GF(2^m)`, `sigma(x, y) = (x^2, y^2)` and negation `(x, y) = (x, x + y)` generate a group of order `2m` that the iteration function respects, so the walk is on ORBITS and two trails have collided when they reach the same orbit -- not the same point. A unit is therefore an orbit, and a piecework block that keyed novelty on a representative would pay `2m` times for one unit.

Second, the weight basis. The distinguishing test and the iteration's branch are both the Hamming weight of x in a NORMAL basis, where sigma is a cyclic rotation of the coordinates; in the polynomial basis neither is orbit-invariant and the walk is not well defined on orbits at all. So the job pins a normal element, the artifact spells x in those coordinates, and the orbit's name is the least rotation of that bit string.

Third, the witness. The step is `R -> R + sigma^j(R) = [1 + s^j]R` and the endomorphism ring is commutative, so a trail of any length is `[mu]R_0` for `mu = prod_j (1 + s^j)^(n_j)` -- and the `n_j` are just how many steps took each branch, in any order. A walker that carries `j_count` counters ships a point anyone verifies with one double scalar multiplication. A walker that carries only the endpoint, which is what a bitsliced client naturally produces, ships something nobody can check for less than the work itself and that anybody can invent for nothing.

family.description: The whole walk shape in one field: the iteration `R -> R + sigma^j(R)`, `j = j_base + ((HW(x) / 2) mod j_count)`; the distinguishing test `HW(x) <= dp_max_weight`; the equivalence group `<-1> x <sigma>`; the orbit name `least rotation of the normal-basis coordinates of x`; and the start point `R_0 = Q + sum_i c_i sigma^i(P)` over the bits of splitmix64(seed). One knob naming all of it rather than five that can contradict each other -- a document that said `equivalence: none` beside a Frobenius-invariant distinguishing test would be describing no walk anyone can run.

poly.description: Reduction polynomial as a bitmask, degree exactly m, irreducible.

order.description: n, the prime order of P; `#E = cofactor * n`.

frobenius_eigenvalue.description:
s with `sigma(R) = [s]R` on `

`, a root of `s^2 - mu*s + 2 = 0 mod n`. Pinned rather than derived because both roots satisfy the equation and only one acts as Frobenius: a job that let each implementation pick would have half of them computing every witness wrong, silently, since the wrong root still produces a well-formed scalar.

nb_generator.description: gamma, a normal element, in polynomial-basis coordinates: the basis `gamma, gamma^2, ..., gamma^(2^(m-1))` is the one weights and orbit names are read in. Pinned by value, not by a rule like 'the type-II generator' or 'the sparsest one', because two implementations that search for it can find different elements and then disagree about which orbit a point is on.

j_base.description: Lowest Frobenius power the iteration adds. ECC2K-130 uses 3.

j_count.description: How many branches, and therefore how many counters a witness carries. ECC2K-130 uses 8.

start_terms.description: Bits of the seed expansion that build the start point, so `R_0 = Q + sum_{i < start_terms} c_i sigma^(i mod m)(P)`.

trail_bits.description: Low bits of the 64-bit seed that count restarts within one unit: `seed = (unit << trail_bits) | trail`. A walker that finishes a trail increments its seed and keeps the unit.

dp_max_weight.description: A point is distinguished when its normal-basis Hamming weight is at most this. Sets both the trail length and the size of the corpus: expected steps per orbit is 1/Pr[HW <= this], and the whole search produces (expected iterations) * Pr orbits. Both matter, in opposite directions -- see docs/design/orbit-piecework.md.

witness.description: How a submitted orbit proves it is a real endpoint. `j-counts`: the artifact carries `j_count` per-branch step counters, and the checker rebuilds `mu = prod_j (1 + s^j)^(n_j)` and requires `[mu*alpha_0]P + [mu]Q` to land on the claimed orbit. An enum with one member on purpose: the obvious alternative -- endpoint and seed only, which is what an unmodified bitsliced client writes -- is not a payable mode at all, because a canonical low-weight bit string costs nothing to invent, and is left out rather than offered with a warning.

max_batch.description: Most orbits one claim may carry. The checker pins it too: it bounds what one submission costs every verifying node.

unit_size.description: Seed slots per unit of the work assignment.

units.description: How many units the seed space divides into, which `work_assignment` maps a node's per-epoch slice onto. At most `2^(64 - trail_bits)`. Advisory, like every assignment in this network: nothing reserves a unit, and a point is paid whichever unit produced it.

max_steps_per_walker.description: Step cap before a trail is abandoned unpaid; 0 means the implementation's default. A capped trail is not a distinguished point and earns nothing -- a client reports it so it can restart the lane, and that report is not a unit.

seed.description: Domain separator XORed into every walk seed before expansion.
